observation: During Rolling Planning Window 2026-10-C and WP-M3D-5 execution, the master orchestrator directly read multi-thousand-line implementation files (tests/m3d_cross_portfolio_test.go) and voluminous test output logs into its own context instead of delegating immediately to bounded worker subagents. This led to master context saturation, severe token consumption, loss of high-level orchestration visibility, and increased vulnerability to attention degradation.
proposed_change: Mandate a strict context admission threshold in AGENTS.md (§2, §3) and docs/PROTOCOLS.md (§11c): Master orchestrators MUST NEVER directly inspect implementation code, edit application files, or parse large test execution logs in their own context. All code inspection, debugging, and iterative test-fixing must be delegated to bounded clean-context implementation subagents.
expected_benefit: Preserves master agent context window for strategic planning, invariant enforcement, and review aggregation; cuts orchestrator token usage by >60%; eliminates context contamination from implementation churn.
possible_counterexamples: Trivial single-line configuration adjustments or reading small status metadata might feel slower if dispatched to a subagent, but the threshold prevents insidious context creep.
evaluation_plan: Evaluate during Planning Window 2026-10-D and Milestone M4: track master orchestrator token consumption and verify zero direct code/test inspections in master session logs.
rollback_plan: Revert delegation clause in AGENTS.md and PROTOCOLS.md to advisory status.
